text: Olha Hennadiivna Kharlan (Ukrainian: Ольга Геннадіївна Харлан; born 4 September 1990) is a Ukrainian sabre fencer also known as Olga Kharlan. She is a four-time individual women's world sabre champion, six-time Olympic medalist, and the most decorated Ukrainian Olympian in history. Kharlan has been ranked #1 in the world in women's sabre for five seasons: 2012–2013, 2013–2014, 2017–2018, 2019–2020, and 2020–2021. She is a two-time team world sabre champion, six-time individual European champion, and two-time team European champion. A five-time Olympian, she won team Olympic gold medals in 2008 and 2024, a team silver medal in 2016, and three individual Olympic bronze medals. Kharlan competed at the 2008 Beijing, 2012 London, 2016 Rio de Janeiro, 2020 Tokyo, and 2024 Paris Olympics. She was inducted into the International Fencing Federation (FIE) Hall of Fame in 2016 and briefly pursued a political career during the early 2010s. Born in Mykolaiv, Ukraine, her father was a sailing and swimming coach who taught her to swim as a baby and also worked as a construction worker and cab driver; her mother worked as a painter and plasterer. Her first interest was samba, cha-cha, and ballroom dancing, but the lessons were too expensive; at age 10, her godfather, sabre coach Anatoly Shlikar, suggested fencing, where lessons were free, and she chose sabre after one year of training. For the first two years, she borrowed equipment from others. She trained under Artem Skorokhod, who was her coach as of 2014, and won her first national Junior title at age 13. She was educated at the Admiral Makarov National University of Shipbuilding in Mykolaiv. She married fellow Ukrainian sabre fencer Dmytro Boiko in 2014, later divorced, and is now married to Italian Olympic sabre fencer Luigi Samele, living in Bologna, Italy. Kharlan joined the Ukrainian national team at age 14 in 2005. Her first international medal was a bronze in the 2005 Junior World Championships in Linz, Austria, and a silver in the team event. She reached the quarter-finals of the 2005 European Fencing Championships in Zalaegerszeg, Hungary, as a cadet. She won four consecutive junior world titles from 2007 to 2010. She placed second in the 2006 European Seniors Fencing Championship in İzmir, Turkey, after losing 14–15 to Sofiya Velikaya of Russia. In 2006–07, she ranked 2nd in the world in women's junior sabre. At age 17, she competed in the 2008 Summer Olympics in Beijing, where Ukraine won the team gold medal, with Kharlan contributing more than half of the team's touches and scoring the decisive touch in the final against China. In the 2008–09 season, she won gold at the 2009 European Fencing Championships in Plovdiv, Bulgaria, in both individual and team events, defeating Russia in the team final. At the 2009 World Fencing Championships in Antalya, she reached the final but lost to Mariel Zagunis of the United States. Ukraine won gold in the team event, defeating France. For this performance, Kharlan and her team were named sportswoman and team of the year at the Ukrainian Heroes of Sports Year ceremony in April 2010. In 2009–10, she won her fourth Junior World Championship in a row, equaling the record of Jacques Brodin, and is the only fencer to have won consecutive junior titles in both individual and team events. She lost in the quarter-finals of the 2010 European Fencing Championships and did not earn a medal, but Ukraine won gold in the team event, defeating Russia again. In 2009–10, she ranked 2nd in the world in women's sabre. She won a gold medal in individual sabre at the 2011 Universiade in Shenzhen, China, and at the 2011 European Fencing Championships in Sheffield, England. In 2010–11, she ranked 3rd in the world in women's sabre. In 2011–12, she ranked 3rd again. In 2012, she won a bronze medal in individual sabre at the London Olympics. At the 2013 World Championships in Budapest, Hungary, she won her first individual world title, defeating Kim Ji-yeon of South Korea 15–14, and then won a second gold in the team event after a comeback in the final against Russia. She also won a gold at the 2013 Universiade in Kazan, Russia. She finished the season ranked #1 in the world for the first time and was inducted into the FIE Hall of Fame. In the 2013–14 season, she won four World Cups out of seven competitions. At the 2014 European Fencing Championships in Strasbourg, France, she won her fourth European gold medal in a row and fifth overall, defeating Dyachenko in the final. In the team event, Ukraine defeated Spain in the quarter-finals 45–43 but lost to France 45–30. Kharlan's contribution was decisive in the match against Poland, earning Ukraine a bronze medal. In March 2014, Ukrainian fencers boycotted the Moscow World Cup in response to the Simferopol incident. In July 2014, they participated in the 2014 World Fencing Championships in Russia. At the 2014 World Fencing Championships in Kazan, Russia, Kharlan won her second individual world title, defeating No. 2 seed Zagunis 15–12. In the team event, Ukraine lost to the United States 44–45 and earned a bronze medal by defeating Italy in the third-place match. Kharlan again came back in the final leg to secure the bronze. She finished the season ranked #1 in the world for the second consecutive year. In 2014–15, she ranked 2nd in the world in women's sabre. At the 2016 Summer Olympics in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, she won a bronze medal in individual sabre, defeating Manon Brunet 15–10, and a silver medal in the team event. She also won individual and team bronze medals at the 2016 European Fencing Championships in Toruń, Poland. In 2015–16, she ranked 3rd in the world in women's sabre. In 2017, at the World Fencing Championships in Leipzig, Germany, she won an individual gold medal. In 2018, she won a team silver medal at the European Fencing Championships in Novi Sad, Serbia. In 2017–18, she was ranked #1 in the world in women's sabre. At the 2019 World Fencing Championships in Budapest, Hungary, she won 15–14 against Sofya Velikaya of Russia, securing her sixth world championship title. She won a gold individual medal at the 2019 European Fencing Championships in Düsseldorf, Germany. In 2018–19, she ranked 2nd in the world in women's sabre. At the 2020 Olympic Games in Tokyo, Japan, she lost to China's Yang Hengyu in the first round. In 2019–20, she was ranked #1 in the world in women's sabre. In 2020–21, she was ranked #1 for the fifth time in her career. She won a team bronze medal at the 2022 European Fencing Championships in Antalya, Turkey. On 27 July 2023, at the 2023 World Fencing Championships in Milan, Italy, a key ranking event for Olympic qualifying, Kharlan defeated Russian Anna Smirnova 15–7. After the bout, Smirnova extended her hand to Kharlan, who offered a blade tap as a salute. Kharlan stated the gesture was a sign of respect for her opponent while acknowledging the ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine. The FIE had suspended handshakes since March 2020, with a public notice stating that blade taps were the accepted alternative. Kharlan said she had been assured by FIE interim president Emmanuel Katsiadakis the day before that a blade tap was acceptable. After Smirnova refused the tap, Kharlan walked away, and Smirnova sat on the strip for 45 minutes and refused to leave, leading to Kharlan being black-carded and eliminated from the individual competition by FIE officials. The disqualification also barred her from competing in the team world championship. This meant she lost the opportunity to earn Olympic qualifying points. Kharlan said she was "screaming in pain" upon hearing the disqualification. Russian fencer Konstantin Lokhanov, who defected to the United States and opposes the Russian invasion, said he believed Smirnova may have set a trap to disqualify Kharlan, noting that blade taps were acceptable during the pandemic and that the Russian fencer had no reason to create drama. Ukrainian tennis player Elina Svitolina, a Wimbledon 2023 semi-finalist who refuses to shake hands with Russian and Belarusian opponents, supported Kharlan and criticized the FIE's decision as "disrespectful" toward Ukrainians, calling for other sports federations to follow the Women's Tennis Association's lead. Ukrainian Minister of Foreign Affairs Dmytro Kuleba urged the FIE to restore Kharlan’s rights. Mykhailo Podolyak, adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky, called the decision "absolutely shameful" and posted a photo showing Smirnova smiling and flashing the victory sign with a Russian soldier, stating she openly admired the Russian army. Kharlan said, "This federation will never change." The Ukrainian Fencing Federation (NFFU) president stated they fully support Kharlan and will appeal the decision because the referee did not issue a black card during the match, and the disqualification came only after the next opponent was determined and after a judge for the match had already made a decision.

Ukrainian fencer Olha Kharlan faced controversy when the International Fencing Federation (FIE) disqualified her from competing at the 2023 World Fencing Championships for refusing to shake hands with a Russian fencer, an action she described as disrespectful towards Ukrainians. Ukrainian Minister of Foreign Affairs Dmytro Kuleba urged the FIE to restore Kharlan’s rights, while Mykhailo Podolyak, adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky, called the decision "absolutely shameful" and shared a photo showing the Russian fencer smiling and flashing the victory sign with a Russian soldier, claiming she openly admired the Russian army. Kharlan stated, "This federation will never change." The Ukrainian Fencing Federation (NFFU) president affirmed full support for Kharlan and argued that the disqualification was not immediate but emerged after the match ended and following the selection of the next opponent and judge, asserting the referee did not issue a direct black card. The following day, IOC President Thomas Bach sent a letter to Kharlan expressing empathy and guaranteeing her a spot in the 2024 Summer Olympics. The FIE, after consulting with the IOC, reversed its decision and reinstated Kharlan for the 2023 World Fencing Championships, though the reversal came too late to allow her to pursue a fifth individual world championship, enabling her only to participate in the team sabre competition. The FIE maintained its stance, asserting the penalty was in full compliance with its rules. Russian Olympic Committee head Stanislav Pozdnyakov accused the IOC of duplicity and picking a side in a political conflict. American author Charlie Pierce noted that both Kharlan and Russian fencer Konstantin Lokhanov were applauded for defending Ukraine, and such stands would continue as the 2024 Olympics approached. On 29 July, Kharlan defeated South Korea’s Choi Se-bin in the women’s sabre individual bronze medal bout, securing Ukraine’s first medal at Paris 2024 and dedicating it to Ukrainian soldiers and athletes killed by Russia. This made her the first Ukrainian female Olympic participant to win medals at four different Olympics. Kharlan became the most awarded Olympian from Ukraine, surpassing swimmer Yana Klochkova, after her team reached the final of the women’s team sabre, defeating South Korea largely due to her 22 touches, winning Ukraine’s first gold medal at the 2024 Summer Olympics. The sabre she used in the Olympics was auctioned for Hr 10 million ($242,000) to support the war effort and purchased by FC Metalist 1925 Kharkiv. In August 2023, Kharlan stated that Russian athletes who publicly oppose Russia’s war against Ukraine have every reason to compete in the 2024 Paris Olympics. She was inducted into the FIE Hall of Fame in 2023 and awarded the Orders of Princess Olga (first, second, and third class), the Ukrainian Orders of Merit (first, second, and third class), the National Legend of Ukraine on 21 August 2024, the Order of Liberty on 23 August 2024, and the title of Ukrainian Honoured Master of Sport. Kharlan was named sportswoman of the year at the Ukrainian Heroes of Sports Year awards in 2009, 2014, 2016, and 2017. In 2008, at 18 years old, she and teammates Olena Khomrova and Olga Zhovnir appeared on the front cover of Ukrainian magazine XXL, which became the top search result for her name by 2012. In 2020, a Barbie doll inspired by Kharlan was launched as part of the Barbie “Role Models” series; in August 2023, she auctioned the only copy on eBay to raise funds for a Ukrainian military rehabilitation clinic. In the 2010 Ukrainian local elections, Kharlan was elected to the Mykolaiv City Council for the Party of Regions despite living in Kyiv, often missing sessions due to fencing commitments. She ran in the October 2012 parliamentary election but was not elected due to being 194th on the Party of Regions list. She left the Party of Regions faction in March 2014 and ran for the Party of Greens of Ukraine in the Kyiv local election in May 2014, failing to meet the 3% threshold and thus not winning any seats; the party listed her third on its 2012 parliamentary election list. During the annexation of Crimea and the 2014 pro-Russian conflict, Kharlan advocated for a united Ukraine. On 17 March 2023, the FIE forced Team USA fencers at the South Korea Fencing World Cup to remove Ukrainian flag ribbons from their hands, prompting Kharlan’s strong protest.
